dialogue:
A: Wow, can you believe what just went down at the World Baseball Classic?

B: I know, right? Venezuela pulling off that upset against Team USA? That’s, like, huge!

A: Seriously! Winning 3-2 and taking home their first title? That’s gotta feel amazing for them.

B: Absolutely! I mean, they were down 2-0 going into the eighth inning, and then bam! Bryce Harper hits that two-run homer. I thought, “Here we go!” 

A: Right? It felt like the tide was turning for a second there. But then, Eugenio Suárez just had to come in with that clutch double in the ninth. What a rollercoaster!

B: Totally! And I was thinking, “Can Team USA really let this slip again?” I mean, two straight runner-up finishes? That’s rough.

A: Yeah, I feel for those guys. They had a powerhouse lineup with Aaron Judge and all, but it just didn’t click in the final. Three hits? That’s... uh, not great.

B: Exactly! And they barely scraped by in pool play, too. Remember how they lost to Italy and it almost knocked them out? 

A: Oh man, don’t remind me! That was like a nail-biter. I was on the edge of my seat watching Italy take down Mexico just to keep Team USA in the game.

B: Right? It was like they were relying on other teams to do them a favor. Not exactly the best strategy if you ask me!

A: Yeah, but you’ve gotta give it to Venezuela for coming back from that semifinal against Italy, too. They really showed some heart.

B: For sure! They were like the underdogs of the tournament. I mean, I love a good underdog story, don’t you?

A: Oh, definitely! It makes it all the more exciting. And now they’ve got their first championship title to show for it. 

B: And I have to say, the atmosphere must have been electric during that final. Miami knows how to throw a party!

A: Haha, right? Speaking of which, did you catch the manager’s comments about moving the WBC to the middle of the MLB season?

B: Yeah, I did! That’s an interesting take. I mean, it could really amp up the excitement, don’t you think?

A: For sure! But then again, it might mess with players' schedules. You know how teams get protective over their star players.

B: True, true. It’s a balancing act for sure. But hey, it’s all about keeping the game fresh and exciting, right?

A: Exactly! And I’m already looking forward to the next WBC. If Venezuela keeps this momentum, who knows what could happen?

B: Oh man, I can't wait! Hopefully, next time, Team USA can bring it home. But hats off to Venezuela for now!

A: Agreed! It’s been a wild ride this year, that’s for sure.

Venezuela upset the Americans 3-2 to win its first World Baseball Classic crown
Venezuela is the champion of the 2026 World Baseball Classic after upsetting Team USA 3-2 in dramatic fashion in Tuesday night's title game.
Venezuela held a 2-0 lead into the eighth inning before Bryce Harper tied things up with a towering two-run home run in the bottom of the frame. But the game wasn't tied for long as Eugenio Suárez slugged a clutch double in the top of the ninth to put Venezuela back in front. Daniel Palencia then shut the door in the bottom of the ninth to seal the first World Baseball Classic title in Venezuela's history and USA's second straight runner-up finish.
Venezuela had to stage a comeback in the semifinals to beat Cinderella story Italy and set up Tuesday's showdown with Team USA, who won a tense 2-1 semifinal showdown against the Dominican Republic on Sunday night in Miami thanks to solo home runs from Gunnar Henderson and Roman Anthony.
The American bats were largely quiet against the D.R., and the story was the same in the title game as a powerhouse lineup that included Aaron Judge, Bobby Witt Jr. and Kyle Schwarber mustered only three hits in a disappointing showing.
